findings.element: report V11 Pünktlichkeit — 'Total' row (tr.punct-row-gesamt) above the 19 displayed Linienbündel rows
findings.claims: A 'Total' row reading Soll 2.101.488 · Ist 2.048.996 · pünktlich 1.861.401 · Delta 52.492 · 90,84%, presented as the total of the table it sits in, with no paginator, no 'showing N of M', no '+ N weitere' row and no other sign that the row list is partial.
findings.actual: The table displays only 19 Linienbündel rows covering 15 TU codes from AAGL to BBA — the alphabet stops at B. Their Soll sums to 152.727, so the Total is 13.8× the visible data. The params chips on the same screen claim 37 TU's / 17 Kantone / All lines, and the raw-data view for the same evaluation reports 4950 entries, so the Total is the full-population figure while the table silently shows a fragment of it.
findings.finding: The Total row aggregates a population 13.8× larger than the rows displayed beneath it, and nothing in the view discloses that the row list is truncated.
findings.user_impact: An analyst computing a TU's share of the network (ARAG 15.854 against a Total of 2.101.488 = 0,75% instead of ~10%) or concluding 'no TU after BBA has a punctuality problem' would report a materially wrong figure to the BAV, because the screen gives no reason to doubt that the visible rows are the whole evaluation.
findings.suggested_fix: Either paginate the bundle table with an explicit '19 von 37 Transportunternehmen' count, or append the prototype's own existing truncation pattern — the '+ 29 weitere Linien' row already used in the chip dropdowns — as the last row of the table, and label the aggregate row 'Total (alle 37 TU)' rather than a bare 'Total'.

evidence.action: Real Chromium (Playwright, /usr/bin/chromium-browser): log in → Auswertungen → 'Anzeigen' on 'Pünktlichkeit – Letzter Monat, Kanton ZH' → dump every tbody row of #view-report-punct with its class and visibility, sum the 19 tr.punct-row-bundle rows column by column, and query the view for any paginator or 'of N' / 'von N' / 'weitere' text.
evidence.observed: 26 tbody rows total: 1 tr.punct-row-gesamt ('Total', 2.101.488 / 2.048.996 / 1.861.401 / 52.492 / 90,84%), 19 tr.punct-row-bundle (AAGL BusÜ 1 … BBA BusÜ 1) and 6 hidden tr.punct-row-line. Sum of the 19 bundles = Soll 152.727 / Ist 149.078 (Total ÷ sum = 13.8×). Paginator query: false. Truncation-text match: [] — no marker of any kind. The params chips on the same screen read '37 TU's', '17 Kantone', 'All lines' while only 15 distinct TU codes (AAGL, AAGR, AAGS, AAGU, AB, ABI, AFA, AMSA, ARAG, ARL, AS, AVA, AVJ, AWA, BBA) appear in the table.

findings.element: Fahrtausfälle report header period (#fa-p-von / #fa-p-bis) vs. the PERIOD cell of its own list row 'Fahrtausfälle DPM – Letzte 7 Tage, SBB'
findings.claims: The evaluations list states this finished evaluation covers 19.05–25.05.2026 (seven days, consistent with its name 'Letzte 7 Tage'). Clicking 'Anzeigen' on that same row opens a report whose params header states 10.06.2026 – 23.06.2026 (fourteen days).
findings.actual: The two indicators read from different sources for the same evaluation: the visible cell is static markup, while showFAReport() reads row.dataset.von/.bis (10.06.2026 / 23.06.2026) and falls back to those same hardcoded literals when the attributes are absent. One of the two statements about which weeks the cancellation figures describe is necessarily wrong, and no report view carries a generation or as-of timestamp that would let the user decide which.
findings.finding: The list and the opened report state two different evaluation periods — a different length and a different month — for the same finished evaluation.
findings.user_impact: An analyst who picked this evaluation because the list said 19.05–25.05.2026 would attribute 33'483 cancelled trips to the wrong two weeks, and could report a May cancellation rate to the BAV using June data, or vice versa.
findings.suggested_fix: Render the list's PERIOD cell from the same data-von/data-bis attributes that showFAReport() reads, so the list cell and the report header cannot diverge, and drop the hardcoded 10.06.2026/23.06.2026 fallback in favour of an explicit 'Zeitraum unbekannt' state.

evidence.action: Real Chromium: log in → read the PERIOD cell and the data-von/data-bis attributes of every openable row → click 'Anzeigen' on 'Fahrtausfälle DPM – Letzte 7 Tage, SBB' → read #fa-eval-name, #fa-p-von, #fa-p-bis in the opened report.
evidence.observed: List row: PERIOD cell '19.05–25.05.2026', attributes von=10.06.2026 bis=23.06.2026. Opened report: title 'Fahrtausfälle DPM – Letzte 7 Tage, SBB', period '10.06.2026 – 23.06.2026'. The other eight openable rows all had matching cell and attributes, so this row is the one that diverges — but the same fallback path (showFAReport, index.html:7239-7240, von='10.06.2026', bis='23.06.2026') would silently mislabel any row whose attributes are missing. No report view (V5, V8, V11) shows a generation timestamp.

findings.element: report V11 Pünktlichkeit — Linienbündel row expander (button.punct-expand-btn, onclick togglePunctBundle(this,0))
findings.claims: The expander ships without the .collapsed class and with a caret glyph reading 'expand_more', and it never carries aria-expanded — so both the class state and the only visible indicator claim the bundle is already open.
findings.actual: The 6 tr.punct-row-line children ship with .punct-hidden, i.e. collapsed. The first click therefore adds .collapsed to re-hide already-hidden rows: the visible row count stays at 20 and nothing on screen changes. Only the second click reveals the 6 line rows (26 rows). The caret stays 'expand_more' in every state, so the control never reports whether it is open or closed.
findings.finding: The expander's class state and caret glyph claim the bundle is expanded while its line rows are hidden, so the first click produces no visible change and the caret never distinguishes open from closed.
findings.user_impact: An analyst drilling into ARAG BusÜ 1 (77,40%, the worst bundle on screen and 12,6 points under the 90% threshold) clicks the caret, sees nothing happen, concludes the bundle has no line-level breakdown, and closes the investigation without ever seeing which line is failing.
findings.suggested_fix: Render the expander with the .collapsed class already applied so its state matches the hidden line rows, and swap the glyph to 'expand_less' plus aria-expanded='true' whenever the rows are visible.

evidence.action: Real Chromium, fresh load each time: log in → 'Anzeigen' on 'Pünktlichkeit – Letzter Monat, Kanton ZH' → probe the first button.punct-expand-btn's class, glyph, aria-expanded and the count of visible tbody rows, then click it four times, probing after each.
evidence.observed: initial: visibleRows=20/26, icon='expand_more', class='punct-expand-btn' (no .collapsed), aria-expanded=null. click 1: visibleRows=20/26 — unchanged — class='punct-expand-btn collapsed', icon still 'expand_more'. click 2: visibleRows=26/26, class back to 'punct-expand-btn', icon still 'expand_more'. click 3: 20/26. click 4: 26/26. The button reported isVisible() && isEnabled() = true throughout, so it is live, not merely present — the first click really is absorbed.

findings.element: report V11 Pünktlichkeit — params chip block (date_range, TU's, Kantone, lines) vs. the table body it introduces
findings.claims: The params header re-states, per evaluation, the period and scope the figures below were computed for — 01.04.2026 – 30.04.2026 / RPV / 37 TU's / 17 Kantone for one evaluation, 01.01.2025 – 31.12.2025 for another.
findings.actual: The header updates with the evaluation; the table does not. Two evaluations one year and one scope apart render a byte-identical Total row and the same 26 rows. renderPunctTable() is called with no period or scope argument, so the params chips describe nothing that is actually applied to the numbers.
findings.finding: Opening two evaluations with different periods and different scopes changes the params header but leaves every figure in the table identical, so the header's scope statement is decorative.
findings.user_impact: Because the numbers never move when the stated period does, an analyst has no way to notice that a report is showing the wrong period's data — which is exactly the mislabelling TRU-2 produces — and would sign off on a 2025 annual figure that is in fact an April 2026 table.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the table from the evaluation's period and scope, or — while there is no backend — mark the figures explicitly as sample data (a 'Demodaten' badge next to the params chips) so a user cannot read them as period-specific.

evidence.action: Real Chromium: log in → 'Anzeigen' on 'Pünktlichkeit – Letzter Monat, Kanton ZH' → capture the params period and the Total row → return to the list → 'Anzeigen' on 'Pünktlichkeit – Letztes Jahr, alle Kantone' → capture both again.
evidence.observed: Evaluation 1 — period '01.04.2026 – 30.04.2026', chips 'RPV / 37 TU's / 17 Kantone', Total '2.101.488 2.048.996 1.861.401 52.492 90,84%', 26 rows. Evaluation 2 — period '01.01.2025 – 31.12.2025', Total '2.101.488 2.048.996 1.861.401 52.492 90,84%', 26 rows. The period text changed; not one digit of the table did. Nine months of Swiss network punctuality and a full calendar year produce the same 2.101.488 scheduled trips.
